Getting started with fiber

Source: vignettes/fiber.qmd

The fiber package provides three S7 classes for representing diffusion MRI tractography data in R:

Class Represents
streamline A single fibre tract (a polyline of 3-D points).
bundle A collection of streamlines (a tractogram / bundle).
bundle_set A collection of bundles (white-matter bundles of a subject, or across subjects / sessions).

Together they let you store geometry, per-point and per-streamline attributes (e.g. fractional anisotropy), and per-bundle or per-set metadata, and they come with a concise set of tools for computing shape descriptors, resampling onto uniform grids, computing the Hausdorff distance, and coercing to and from the dwiFiber S4 class of the dti package.

This vignette walks through the core workflow. A companion, technical vignette (fiber-api) describes the complete API in detail.

Building a streamline

A streamline stores a $P \times 3$ matrix of coordinates. The columns must be named "X", "Y", and "Z".

# A helix in 3-D, sampled at 50 points
t <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 50)
sl <- streamline(
  points = cbind(X = cos(t), Y = sin(t), Z = t / (2 * pi))
)
sl
#> 
#> ── Object of class `fiber::streamline()` with 50 points. ──
#> 
#> • Point attributes: none
#> • Streamline attributes: none
#>

You can attach per-point attributes (e.g. fractional anisotropy) via point_data and per-streamline scalars (e.g. a mean FA or a label) via streamline_data:

sl <- streamline(
  points = cbind(X = cos(t), Y = sin(t), Z = t / (2 * pi)),
  point_data = list(FA = runif(50)),
  streamline_data = list(mean_FA = mean(runif(50)), label = "helix")
)
sl@n_points # 50
#> [1] 50
sl@point_attributes # "FA"
#> [1] "FA"
sl@streamline_attributes # c("mean_FA", "label")
#> [1] "mean_FA" "label"

Shape descriptors

Functions like get_curvilinear_length(), get_sinuosity(), and get_euclidean_length() compute scalar shape descriptors from the geometry:

get_curvilinear_length(sl)
#> [1] 6.358015
get_sinuosity(sl)
#> [1] 6.358015

get_curvature() and get_torsion() return a per-point profile along the arc-length abscissa:

head(get_curvature(sl))
#> [1] 1.537338e-05 1.625127e-02 4.592627e-02 8.636675e-02 1.352354e-01
#> [6] 1.906608e-01

add_shape_descriptors() attaches several descriptors to an object at once. Scalar descriptors land in @streamline_data; per-point ones (curvature, torsion) land in @point_data:

sl2 <- add_shape_descriptors(sl)
sl2@streamline_data$euclidean_length
#> [1] 1
head(sl2@point_data$curvature)
#> [1] 1.537338e-05 1.625127e-02 4.592627e-02 8.636675e-02 1.352354e-01
#> [6] 1.906608e-01

Bundling streamlines

Wrap a list of streamlines in a bundle. Any @streamline_data keys common to all streamlines are lifted automatically into bundle@streamline_data as length-S vectors:

sl_a <- streamline(points = cbind(X = cos(t), Y = sin(t), Z = t / (2 * pi)))
sl_b <- streamline(
  points = cbind(X = 1.1 * cos(t), Y = 1.1 * sin(t), Z = t / (2 * pi))
)
b <- bundle(streamlines = list(sl_a, sl_b))
b
#> 
#> ── Object of class `fiber::bundle()` with 2 streamliness and [50–50] points per streamline. ──
#> 
#> • Point attributes: none
#> • Streamline attributes: none
#> • Bundle attributes: none
#> 
b@n_streamlines # 2
#> [1] 2
b@streamline_data$mean_FA # lifted automatically, if present
#> NULL

You can mix streamlines and bundles with bind_bundles():

b2 <- bind_bundles(sl_a, b)
b2@n_streamlines # 3
#> [1] 3

Reparametrisation

reparametrize() resamples streamlines onto a uniform arc-length grid using linear interpolation. A single streamline can be resampled to any number of points; by default a bundle is resampled to the rounded mean number of points across its streamlines:

sl_20 <- reparametrize(sl_a, n_points = 20L)
sl_20@n_points # 20
#> [1] 20

b_20 <- reparametrize(b, n_points = 20L)
b_20[[1]]@n_points # 20
#> [1] 20
b_20[[2]]@n_points # 20
#> [1] 20

Hausdorff distance

compute_hausdorff_distance() computes the symmetric Hausdorff distance between streamlines. Depending on the inputs, it returns a scalar, a vector, or a dist object:

# streamlines -> scalar
compute_hausdorff_distance(sl_a, sl_b)
#> [1] 0.1

# bundle (with no second argument) -> pairwise dist object
d <- compute_hausdorff_distance(b)
as.matrix(d)
#>     1   2
#> 1 0.0 0.1
#> 2 0.1 0.0

# bundle vs streamline -> vector
compute_hausdorff_distance(b, sl_a)
#> [1] 0.0 0.1

The core pairwise computation runs in C++ (via cpp11) for speed.

Bundle sets

A bundle_set collects bundle objects. Two use cases are equally well supported: grouping the multiple white-matter bundles of a single subject, or grouping bundles across subjects / sessions. Names of the input list (like "callosum" or "sub-01") are transferred into bundle_set@bundle_data as the id_from_input_names attribute:

# Single subject: several white-matter bundles of one subject
bs_single <- bundle_set(list(
  callosum = bundle(list(sl_a)),
  arcuate = bundle(list(sl_b))
))
bs_single
#> 
#> ── Object of class `fiber::bundle_set()` with 2 bundles and [1–1] streamlines per bundle. ──
#> 
#> • Point attributes: none
#> • Streamline attributes: none
#> • Bundle attributes: "id_from_input_names"
#> • Set attributes: none
#> 
bs_single@n_bundles # 2
#> [1] 2
bs_single[["callosum"]] # extract one bundle (push-down)
#> 
#> ── Object of class `fiber::bundle()` with 1 streamlines and [50–50] points per streamline. ──
#> 
#> • Point attributes: none
#> • Streamline attributes: none
#> • Bundle attributes: "id_from_input_names"
#> 

# Multi-subject: the same bundle across two subjects / sessions
b_sub01 <- bundle(
  streamlines = list(sl_a),
  bundle_data = list(subject = "sub-01")
)
b_sub02 <- bundle(
  streamlines = list(sl_b),
  bundle_data = list(subject = "sub-02")
)

bs <- bundle_set(list("sub-01" = b_sub01, "sub-02" = b_sub02))
bs
#> 
#> ── Object of class `fiber::bundle_set()` with 2 bundles and [1–1] streamlines per bundle. ──
#> 
#> • Point attributes: none
#> • Streamline attributes: none
#> • Bundle attributes: "subject" and "id_from_input_names"
#> • Set attributes: none
#> 
bs@bundle_data$subject # c("sub-01", "sub-02")
#> [1] "sub-01" "sub-02"
bs[["sub-01"]] # extract one subject (push-down)
#> 
#> ── Object of class `fiber::bundle()` with 1 streamlines and [50–50] points per streamline. ──
#> 
#> • Point attributes: none
#> • Streamline attributes: none
#> • Bundle attributes: "subject" and "id_from_input_names"
#>

bundle_set objects also support reparametrize() and add_shape_descriptors(), which operate per bundle and preserve @bundle_data / @bundle_set_data.

A real corpus callosum tractogram

The package ships a real tractogram from the corpus callosum (inst/extdata/CC_SingleTensor.csv): 100 streamlines, each a sequence of 3-D points with a per-point fractional anisotropy (FA) value. The file reads straight into a bundle, grouping points by StreamlineId and keeping FA as a per-point attribute:

cc <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "CC_SingleTensor.csv", package = "fiber"),
  header = TRUE
)

make_streamline <- function(d) {
  d <- d[order(d$PointId), ]
  streamline(
    points = as.matrix(d[c("X", "Y", "Z")]),
    point_data = list(FA = d$FA)
  )
}
cc_bundle <- bundle(
  streamlines = lapply(split(cc, cc$StreamlineId), make_streamline)
)

cc_bundle@n_streamlines # 100
#> [1] 100
cc_bundle[[1]]@n_points # 150
#> [1] 150
cc_bundle[[1]]@point_attributes # "FA"
#> [1] "FA"
range(cc_bundle[[1]]@point_data$FA) # per-point FA on the first stream
#> [1] 0.1284090 0.9019012

The FA per-point attribute is present on every streamline, so FA is a shared point attribute across the whole tractogram: cc_bundle[[1]]@point_attributes returns "FA" for each of the 100 streamlines. To summarise anisotropy per streamline, lift a scalar (e.g. per-streamline mean FA) into @streamline_data; the constructor then carries it automatically:

cc_bundle2 <- bundle(
  streamlines = lapply(
    split(cc, cc$StreamlineId),
    function(d) {
      d <- d[order(d$PointId), ]
      streamline(
        points = as.matrix(d[c("X", "Y", "Z")]),
        point_data = list(FA = d$FA),
        streamline_data = list(mean_FA = mean(d$FA))
      )
    }
  )
)
cc_bundle2@streamline_data$mean_FA
#>   [1] 0.5795448 0.5845522 0.5952879 0.5946678 0.5892372 0.5769750 0.5765600
#>   [8] 0.5754540 0.5867316 0.5914767 0.5528441 0.5635257 0.5591195 0.5995738
#>  [15] 0.6122286 0.6092749 0.5864019 0.5680139 0.5614040 0.5859508 0.5926974
#>  [22] 0.5859467 0.6018204 0.6175521 0.6333238 0.6412199 0.6390573 0.6170749
#>  [29] 0.5898951 0.5745954 0.5674078 0.5720140 0.5863193 0.5993463 0.5945758
#>  [36] 0.5873722 0.5704101 0.5940291 0.6021282 0.6058955 0.6183781 0.6173499
#>  [43] 0.6073979 0.5886485 0.5873168 0.5755910 0.6447720 0.6571459 0.6438632
#>  [50] 0.6567112 0.6604739 0.6523562 0.6442567 0.6524128 0.6537668 0.6484673
#>  [57] 0.6408378 0.6184391 0.5746873 0.5702121 0.6325441 0.6638909 0.6736785
#>  [64] 0.6715991 0.6649784 0.6660586 0.6615916 0.6666470 0.6515800 0.6453447
#>  [71] 0.6349435 0.6328630 0.6655557 0.6633166 0.6620502 0.6631885 0.6670419

mean(cc_bundle2@streamline_data$mean_FA) # mean across the 100 streamlines
#> [1] 0.6158391

Interoperability with the dti package

If the dti package is installed, you can coerce fiber objects to and from its dwiFiber S4 class:

if (requireNamespace("dti", quietly = TRUE)) {
  dfi <- as_dwifiber(b)
  class(dfi) # "dwiFiber"
  b_back <- as_bundle(dfi)
  b_back@n_streamlines
}
#> [1] 2

as_dwifiber() uses per-point directions stored in @point_data (direction_x, direction_y, direction_z) when present, otherwise it estimates them from the coordinates via finite differences.

If dti emits an rgl warning ('rgl.init' failed, X11 error, …) when you run the coercion above, that comes from dti loading the rgl package and failing to open a graphics display in your environment. It is unrelated to the fiber package — the conversion itself is unaffected.
